topics.title: Meet the Ukulele
topics.short: The parts of a ukulele, the four sizes, and the four strings, G, C, E and A, with the high G that gives the ukulele its sound.

topics.title: Where the Ukulele Comes From
topics.short: How a small Portuguese instrument, the machete, arrived in Hawaiʻi in 1879 and became the ʻukulele, with the help of three Madeiran craftsmen and King Kalākaua.

topics.title: Holding the Ukulele
topics.short: How to sit or stand with a ukulele, where each hand goes, how to press a string cleanly, and how to look after your hands while you learn.

topics.title: Tuning G C E A
topics.short: Tune your ukulele with the tuner, by ear from reference notes, or string to string with the 5th, 4th and 7th frets.

topics.title: Reading Chord Charts
topics.short: How to read a ukulele chord diagram: the strings, the frets, the dots and finger numbers, open strings, and what the left-handed view changes.

topics.title: Reading Tab
topics.short: Ukulele tablature: four lines for four strings, numbers for frets, and the rhythm written under the tab. With notation above it, so you can learn both.

topics.title: First Chords: C and Am
topics.short: Your first two chords, C and A minor, each with one finger, and your first song-length practice: four down strums per chord.

topics.title: F and G7: Three Chords, Many Songs
topics.short: Add F and G7 to C, the three chords of the key of C, and practice changing between them in time.

topics.title: Strumming Down and Up
topics.short: Eighth-note strumming: down on the beat, up on the “and,” with a hand that never stops moving. Plus misses, the key to every strum pattern.

topics.title: The Island Strum
topics.short: The ukulele’s best-loved strum: down, down-up, (miss), up-down-up. Learn it in pieces, then play it with C, Am, F and G7.

topics.title: Picking a Tune
topics.short: Play single notes: the notes of the first three frets, picking with the thumb or index finger, and your first tunes from tab.

topics.title: G, D7 and Em: the Key of G
topics.short: The G chord, D7 and E minor: the main chords of the key of G, with tips for the trickier shapes and a song in G.

topics.title: Waltz Time: Three Beats to a Bar
topics.short: Songs in 3/4 time and how to strum them: the waltz pattern with a thumb note on beat 1, a busier version with up strums, and a pickup note.

topics.title: The Hawaiian Vamp
topics.short: The little chord turn that starts, ends and links so many Hawaiian songs: D7–G7–C in C, A7–D7–G in G. Learn it, hear why it works, and play a tune that ends with it.

topics.title: Finding Notes on the Fretboard
topics.short: Half steps and whole steps on one string, sharps and flats, the 12th fret octave, and a way to find any note on the ukulele’s neck.

topics.title: The Major Scale
topics.short: The major scale’s pattern of whole and half steps, the C and G major scales on the ukulele, and how scales connect to the chords you know.

topics.title: Minor Keys and Minor Chords
topics.short: Minor chords and the minor keys: Am, Dm and E7 in A minor; Em, Am and B7 in E minor; and how a major chord becomes minor.

topics.title: Barre Chords and Movable Shapes
topics.short: Lay one finger across several strings: B♭, Bm and B7, and how one shape slid up the neck gives you a whole family of chords.

topics.title: Low-G Tuning
topics.short: Swap the high G string for a low one: what changes, what stays the same, and the extra notes it gives you for tunes.

topics.title: The Chunk and More Strums
topics.short: The chunk (a muted, percussive strum), accents, the 6/8 lilt and a swung shuffle: four ways to give your strumming more rhythm and color.

topics.title: Fingerpicking
topics.short: Pick the strings one at a time with thumb and fingers: one finger per string, three picking patterns, and a fingerpicked waltz.

topics.title: Tune and Chord Together
topics.short: Chord melody: play the tune as the top note of each chord, so one ukulele carries both. The first phrase of Amazing Grace, worked out step by step.

topics.title: Ragtime-Era Ukulele
topics.short: The ukulele craze of the 1910s and 1920s: swung strums, the ragtime chord chain E7–A7–D7–G7–C, and Scott Joplin’s The Entertainer on four strings.

topics.title: Hawaiian Songs
topics.short: The songs of Queen Liliʻuokalani and King Kalākaua, Hawaiʻi Ponoʻī and Hawaiʻi Aloha, the old D tuning, and how to play Hawaiian music with respect. With the chords of Aloha ʻOe to strum.
